post_understanding.summary: A view in SQL Server 2012 using a correlated subquery against BidHistory to find the latest DTStamp per (SKU, campaginid) and a WHERE predicate on a left-joined column runs slowly. Comments note the WHERE predicate converts the left joins to inner joins, and the accepted answer suggests rewriting with ROW_NUMBER and moving the predicate into the join.
symptoms: execution plan indicates optimizer treats left joins as inner joins
derived table uses correlated MAX(DTStamp) per (SKU, campaginid)
suspected_root_causes: inefficient pattern for 'latest per group' using a correlated subquery against BidHistory
missing composite index on BidHistory (SKU, campaginid, DTStamp DESC) to support latest lookup
filter on a left-joined column in WHERE effectively forcing inner join semantics
possible data skew with many BidHistory rows per (SKU, campaginid)
key_evidence: Original view: correlated subquery SELECT MAX(DTStamp) FROM BidHistory WHERE campaginid = ph1.campaginid AND ph1.SKU = SKU
Comment: 'WHERE (maxcpc - dervtable.Bid <> 0) converts your left joins back to inner joins'
Answer suggests ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY SKU, campaginid ORDER BY DTStamp DESC) and moving predicate to join
assumptions: DBMS is SQL Server 2012 or compatible (based on tags).
No suitable composite index exists on BidHistory to support the 'latest per group' lookup.
BidHistory is significantly larger than the other tables and contains many rows per (SKU, campaginid).
Data cardinalities are large enough to make the correlated subquery expensive (e.g., 1M+ BidHistory rows).
The slow query is run as a standalone report/workload without heavy concurrent background activity.
Column names and the misspelling 'campaginid' are as shown and used consistently in schema.
Numeric types: maxcpc and Bid are decimals and comparisons are sargable; time type is datetime/datetime2.

anomaly_injection.name: define_view_with_correlated_max_and_where_filter
anomaly_injection.target: dbo.ReSyncAdwords view over dbo.currentadwordsmaxbid, dbo.WebSkuLookup, dbo.BidHistory
anomaly_injection.method: Create a schemabound view that left-joins to a derived table built via a correlated subquery selecting MAX(DTStamp) for each (SKU, campaginid), and applies WHERE (maxcpc - dervtable.Bid <> 0).

parameters.view_definition: CREATE VIEW dbo.ReSyncAdwords WITH SCHEMABINDING AS SELECT cab.maxcpc - d.Bid AS Expr1, cab.webid, cab.maxcpc, cab.adgroupid, cab.keywordid, d.SKU, d.Bid, cab.campaginid FROM dbo.currentadwordsmaxbid AS cab LEFT OUTER JOIN dbo.WebSkuLookup AS wsl ON cab.webid = wsl.webid LEFT OUTER JOIN ( SELECT ph1.SKU, ph1.Bid, ph1.Channel, ph1.DTStamp, ph1.campaginid FROM dbo.BidHistory AS ph1 WHERE ph1.DTStamp = ( SELECT MAX(ph2.DTStamp) FROM dbo.BidHistory AS ph2 WHERE ph2.campaginid = ph1.campaginid AND ph2.SKU = ph1.SKU ) ) AS d ON wsl.sku = d.SKU AND cab.campaginid = d.campaginid WHERE (cab.maxcpc - d.Bid <> 0);
parameters.note: This mirrors the original slow pattern and WHERE predicate that effectively enforces inner join semantics.

safety_notes: Ensure view creation is reversible (DROP VIEW) after testing.

anomaly_injection.name: omit_supporting_composite_index_on_BidHistory
anomaly_injection.method: Do not create a composite index on (SKU, campaginid, DTStamp DESC) to force scans/inefficient lookups for latest rows.
safety_notes: If any default or pre-existing indexes exist in the test environment, drop them only in the test database.

metrics.expected_change: increase (e.g., > 5000 ms on the generated dataset)
increase relative to a ROW_NUMBER/indexed approach
plan shows expensive operations deriving latest per group (e.g., Nested Loops with repeated scans or Hash/Stream Aggregate feeding a join)

query_or_transaction_effects: SELECT from dbo.ReSyncAdwords completes slowly due to high CPU and I/O work on BidHistory.
The WHERE predicate (maxcpc - d.Bid <> 0) causes the optimizer to treat left joins as inner joins, so rows with no matching BidHistory are excluded.
validation_criteria: On the defined dataset without the composite index, the view query takes noticeably longer than 5 seconds and shows high logical reads from BidHistory.
The actual execution plan indicates that the derived table for latest per (SKU, campaginid) causes large scans/aggregations.

Adding a composite index on BidHistory (SKU, campaginid, DTStamp DESC) INCLUDE (Bid, Channel) and/or rewriting with ROW_NUMBER should reduce duration and logical reads by a large factor (>3x), confirming the root cause was the inefficient pattern/missing index.
